name: Vriddhagireeswarar Temple, Vriddhachalam
deity: Shiva as Vriddhagireeswarar (Pazhamalainathar), with the goddess Vriddhambikai (Periyanayaki)
period: Great ancient temple of the Nadu Nadu region, the Tirumudukunram of the Tevaram, sung by Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar (7th to 8th century); major Chola-period building with an inscription of 982 CE and later additions
dynasty: Chola (queen Sembiyan Mahadevi, 10th century), with later Pandya and other additions
summary: Vriddhagireeswarar, the Lord of the Ancient Hill, is the great Shiva temple of Vriddhachalam, the Tirumudukunram of the Tevaram, praised by all three saints and remembered for the story of Sundarar's gold, a river that gave it up and a tank that returned it.

sections.history: Vriddhachalam, the Tirumudukunram of the Tevaram, is one of the largest and oldest Shiva temples of the Nadu Nadu region, praised by Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar. Its name speaks of antiquity: vriddha is old and achala a hill, and the town is also called Vriddha Kasi, held in local belief to be older even than Kashi. Tradition names the sage Vipachit as its earliest builder. The temple standing today is generally dated to the Chola period, and an inscription from the reign of Uttama Chola, dated 982 CE, records that parts were raised by the queen Sembiyan Mahadevi, who is credited with the central shrine, the covered verandas and the shrines of the lesser deities. Later rulers, including the Pandyas, made further additions. The Lord is praised by five names in the tradition, Vriddhagireeswarar, Pazhamalainathar, Vriddhachaleswarar, Mudhukundreeswarar and Vriddhagiri, and the goddess is Vriddhambikai, also called Periyanayaki and Balambikai.
sections.architecture: The temple is a great enclosure of three concentric courts, with tall towers of seven storeys. The oldest rises at the entrance to the second court, and four more stand at the middle points of the outer walls; tradition names one of these gateways after Gandaraditya Chola, the husband of Sembiyan Mahadevi. In front of the sanctum the flagstaff is attended by five Nandis, named for Indra, the Vedas, the soul, wealth and dharma. One mandapam is carved in the form of a chariot. Near the inner shrine is the Vinayaka known as Mattru Uraitha Vinayaka, the Ganesha who tested the gold. The sacred waters include the Manimuktha river and the Agni, Kubera and Chakra teerthams, and the sacred tree of the temple is the vanni.
sections.legends: Vriddhachalam's oldest story is of the hill itself. It is said that Brahma, making the world from the waters, used the remains of the demons Madhu and Kaitabha, slain by Vishnu, to raise hills, and so crowded the earth that he did not know that Shiva had taken the form of a mountain. Shiva then gathered the hills into one great mountain, the first and eldest of all, and so the place is held to have survived the great dissolution. The best-loved story is Sundarar's. He was gathering funds at Tiruvarur to feed devotees on Panguni Uthiram, and the Lord of this temple gave him twelve thousand gold coins. Fearing robbers on the road, the saint cast the coins into the Manimuktha river here, and, on his order, they were taken up from the tank at Tiruvarur. From this comes the Tamil saying of losing in the river and searching in the tank. The Vinayaka who bore witness to the purity of the gold is honoured as Mattru Uraitha Vinayaka. These are told as tradition.
sections.festivals: The great festival is the ten-day Brahmotsavam in the month of Masi, in February or March, with the car festival on the ninth day, when crowds gather from across the region. A ten-day Vasanthotsavam is held in Vaikasi, in May or June, and Aani Tirumanjanam, Arudra Darshan and Skanda Sashti are also observed. Girivalam, the circumambulation, is made on the full-moon days, and Maha Shivaratri and the monthly Pradosham are kept as at every Shiva temple. Confirm dates locally, as they follow the Tamil calendar.
sections.experience: Vriddhachalam asks for time. Enter through the great gateway and walk the courts slowly, noting the five Nandis at the flagstaff, the chariot mandapam and the towers rising on every side, before coming to Vriddhagireeswarar in the sanctum and to Vriddhambikai in her shrine. Look for the Mattru Uraitha Vinayaka and recall Sundarar's story of the gold. Because this is a large temple of a busy town, the courts are lively on festival days, and a quiet morning visit lets the age of the place be felt. Many devotees also make the Girivalam walk around the temple on full-moon days.

visit.timings: Typically open in the morning and again from late afternoon into the evening, with a midday break; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected: dhotis or trousers for men, sarees, salwar kameez, or long skirts for women, with shoulders and knees covered. Footwear is left at the entrance stands.
visit.photography: Photography is generally permitted in the outer corridors and courtyards but prohibited inside the inner sanctum, in keeping with Tamil Nadu temple rules. Ask temple staff before photographing rituals or priests.
visit.gettingThere: Vriddhachalam, called Virudhachalam in modern use, is a town in Cuddalore district on the railway line between Chennai and Tiruchirappalli, about 215 km from Chennai, and it has a railway station and bus services from many parts of Tamil Nadu. The temple stands in the heart of the town. Panruti and Ulundurpettai are the nearby towns. The nearest major airports are Tiruchirappalli and Chennai. Confirm local transport and timings before travelling.
